To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

schools are increasingly adopting mass customization strategies to cope with the 'diversity efficiency dilemma', and that the adoption of these strategies may cause a mismatch between what schools offer and what students need and want.

Dutch secondary schools are increasingly differentiating their educational offerings along a limited number of dimensions, that they apply'mass customized' strategies to add variety without increasing costs, that they are not always aware of the contradictions and risks involved in these practices, and that the'mass customization' practices they apply are closely linked to organizational and managerial strategies pursued by these schools.

Dutch schools apply'mass customization', i.e. differentiation strategies that aim at adding diversity without adding costs, to cope with the 'diversity efficiency dilemma'; these strategies are closely related to organizational strategies pursued; the risks and inherent contradiction of these strategies are that while government policies and school seek to put the individual students at the center of the education system, the inevitable diversity-efficiency dilemma may cause many students to get what they did not ask for.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether schools are capable of providing a truly 'customized' education for all students.
the extent to which schools, as organizations, are able to meet the diversity needs of their customers.
the question whether the'mass customized' education that schools offer to students is really what students want.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
schools do not apply mass customization strategies, but that they do so only to a limited extent.
the mass customization strategies applied in schools may be effective in terms of cost efficiency but are not always in line with the needs of students.
schools are in fact not customer oriented, but rather customer driven.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mass customization strategies of schools are a means to an end.
the Dutch schools are in fact trying to implement mass customization in the educational sector, but the results are not always positive.
we have been able to demonstrate that the Dutch educational system is in transition towards mass customization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
schools should be careful not to confuse the needs of students with the needs of the school.
the 'one size fits all' approach to education has been replaced by a 'one size fits some' approach, with the 'one size' being a school's organizational strategy.
schools are in the same boat as other organizations that are trying to cope with diversity.
